nodes.content: Recover camera motion and independently moving rigid-object geometry from monocular video while distinguishing focal-length changes from scene motion.
requirements: Reduce scale-aligned reconstruction error by 20% versus fixed-intrinsics multibody reconstruction on variable-focal-length sequences.
Characterize observational ambiguities and achieve 90% empirical coverage for predicted geometry confidence regions.

nodes.content: Jointly optimize spline focal length, camera and rigid-object poses, and geometry from background/object tracks; report ambiguities and bootstrap geometry intervals.
When do background parallax and object tracks distinguish focal-length drift from forward camera motion and object translation?
With ≥2° background parallax and ≥1.5× depth spread, estimated focal drift has <5% error despite forward motion and moving objects.
Sweep background parallax, depth spread, zoom, and forward/object motion in ZoomRigid; measure focal error, reconstruction error, and interval coverage.
Render 480 ZoomRigid sequences straddling 2° parallax and 1.5× depth spread with forward/object motion; measure focal-drift error.
On 120 qualifying ZoomRigid sequences with forward/object motion, median focal-drift error was 11%, exceeding the predicted 5%.
With ≥2° parallax, ≥1.5× depth spread, ≥5% depth-normalized lateral baseline, and ≥60% static tracks, median focal-drift error should be <5%.
Stratify qualifying ZoomRigid sequences by 5% depth-normalized lateral baseline and 60% static tracks; measure median focal-drift error.
Among 48 ZoomRigid sequences meeting both added thresholds, median focal-drift error was 4.3%, versus 14% for the other 72.
On n8's 48 identifiable ZoomRigid sequences, benchmark scale-aligned geometry error against fixed intrinsics and measure 90% bootstrap-region coverage.
ZoomRigid-48 benchmark report with scale-aligned geometry errors versus fixed intrinsics, empirical coverage of nominal 90% bootstrap regions, and ambiguity strata.
Does variable-focal fitting cut scale-aligned geometry error ≥20% versus fixed intrinsics and achieve ≥90% coverage of nominal 90% bootstrap regions?
Use the ZoomRigid-48 report as adoption gate: ≥20% geometry-error reduction and ≥90% coverage, restricted to identifiable sequences.
Use zoom-change-point priors and projective-gauge diagnostics to separate focal jumps from rigid motion and widen geometry intervals under ambiguity.
Fit focal change-points, profile projective gauges, inflate gauge-sensitive intervals, and benchmark scale-aligned error versus fixed intrinsics and coverage.
Using ZoomRigid-48 report's ambiguity strata, calibrate focal change-point penalties and gauge-profiled geometry intervals on 96 disjoint ZoomRigid sequences.
ZoomGauge-v1 calibration package containing fitted change-point penalties, gauge-profiled geometry intervals, and ambiguity-stratified thresholds from 96 disjoint ZoomRigid sequences.
Benchmark ZoomGauge-v1 against spline-focal and fixed-intrinsics reconstruction on 120 held-out ZoomRigid clips; measure scale-aligned error and ambiguity-stratified 90%-interval coverage.
On 120 held-out ZoomRigid clips, spline-focal lowered scale-aligned geometry error 23% versus fixed intrinsics with 91% coverage; ZoomGauge-v1: 12%, 83%.
Reject ZoomGauge-v1 on held-out clips; defer spline-focal adoption until identifiable-subset results satisfy the adoption gate.
Does ZoomGauge-v1's change-point prior mistake gradual zoom for object motion, explaining its weaker geometry reduction and 83% coverage?
On gradual-zoom clips, disabling change-point penalties reduces object-translation error ≥15% and raises nominal 90% geometry coverage to ≥90%.
Ablate ZoomGauge-v1 change-point penalties on 60 held-out gradual-zoom clips; compare object-translation error and nominal 90% geometry-region coverage.
Anchor multibody bundle adjustment with focal estimates from orthogonal vanishing points; calibrate geometry intervals by resampling line detections.
Can background orthogonal vanishing points constrain focal drift when moving-object lines contaminate detections and the principal point is uncertain?
On 80 Manhattan-world ZoomRigid clips, vary moving-object line contamination (0–40%) and principal-point error (±20 pixels); measure vanishing-point focal-drift error.
Penalty ablation cut translation error 18% and raised coverage to 91%; vanishing-point focal error reached 13% at 40% contamination.
At 40% object-line contamination, unfiltered vanishing-point anchors exceed 10% focal-drift error, making background-line filtering necessary.
On 40 held-out Manhattan-world clips at 40% line contamination, compare unfiltered versus tracked-background-only vanishing-point focal-drift errors.
On 40 held-out clips at 40% contamination, unfiltered focal-drift error was 7.8%, versus 8.1% with background-only filtering.
At ±20-pixel principal-point offsets, focal-drift error exceeds 10% regardless of line filtering; at ≤5-pixel offsets, it stays below 9%.
Given contamination sensitivity and ineffective line filtering, test ±5/20-pixel principal-point offsets on held-out Manhattan-world clips; compare filtered/unfiltered focal-drift errors.
At ±20-pixel principal-point offsets, focal-drift error was 12.4% unfiltered and 11.9% filtered; at ≤5 pixels, 7.1% and 7.5%.
Using n30's offset strata, measure filtered and unfiltered focal-drift errors on 60 independent Manhattan clips at ≤5- and ±20-pixel offsets.
On 60 independent Manhattan clips, ±20-pixel offsets yielded 8.6% unfiltered and 8.4% filtered focal-drift error, contradicting >10%.
At ±20-pixel principal-point offsets, ≥30° projected vanishing-direction separation keeps focal-drift error <9% despite 40% object-line contamination.
Render matched Manhattan clips above/below 30° vanishing-direction separation; impose ±20-pixel offsets and 40% contamination, then compare focal-drift errors.
Reconcile n30/n32 using 80 matched Manhattan clips at ±20-pixel offsets and 40% contamination; compare focal-drift errors above/below 30° separation.
On 80 matched clips, ≥30° separation yielded 7.9% focal-drift error versus 13.2% below 30°, with ±20-pixel offsets and 40% contamination.
Test n36's ≥30° threshold on 100 independent Manhattan clips at ±20-pixel offsets and 40% contamination; measure focal-drift error.
Manhattan-100 validation report with separation-stratified focal-drift errors, principal-point offsets, contamination labels, and confidence intervals.
Adopt ≥30° separation for vanishing-point anchors only if Manhattan-100 confirms <9% focal-drift error; otherwise disable anchors.
Fuse pretrained object-shape priors with silhouette-based multibody bundle adjustment to distinguish zoom from motion; calibrate geometry intervals conformally.
When silhouettes expand, can shape priors separate zoom from approaching objects without under-covering unseen-category geometry?
With ≥3 tracked objects, shape-prior fitting keeps zoom-versus-approach misclassification below 10%, while conformal geometry regions cover ≥90% unseen-category shapes.
Use ZoomGauge-v1 thresholds to stratify 120 unseen-category clips with ≥3 objects; measure shape-prior zoom/approach misclassification, geometry error, and conformal coverage.
Across 120 unseen-category clips, shape priors misclassified zoom/approach 8%, reduced scale-aligned geometry error 22% versus fixed intrinsics, with 91% coverage.
Prioritize shape-prior fitting for ≥3-object unseen-category clips (22% error reduction, 91% coverage) after rejecting ZoomGauge-v1.
Estimate zoom from background-line curvature under focal-dependent radial distortion, then reconstruct rigid bodies with ambiguity-stratified conformal geometry intervals.
Fit coupled focal-length/distortion trajectories from background lines, optimize multibody geometry, and calibrate 90% intervals across line-density strata.
Implement CurvZoom-v1: gate vanishing anchors per n39, include n44's shape priors, and fit focal-distortion multibody geometry from background-line curvature.
CurvZoom-v1 implementation containing gated vanishing-point anchors, shape-prior initialization, coupled focal-distortion bundle adjustment, and line-density-stratified conformal geometry intervals.
Benchmark CurvZoom-v1 on 150 held-out variable-focal clips across line-density strata; compare fixed-intrinsics geometry error and nominal 90% interval coverage.
On 150 held-out clips, CurvZoom-v1 reduced scale-aligned geometry error 24% versus fixed intrinsics; nominal 90% intervals covered 91.3%.
Adopt CurvZoom-v1 with n39's conditional anchor gate and n44's shape priors: 24% error reduction, 91.3% coverage.
